\section{The conceptual tensions}

\begin{longtable}{p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.36\textwidth}p{0.35\textwidth}}
\toprule
Tension & Lesson & Strategic response\\
\midrule
\endhead
Gauge invariance versus locality & Individual staples are covariant rather
than invariant; their mutual dispersion is invariant. & Use local covariant
coordinates together with invariant relational functionals.\\
\addlinespace
Coarse-graining versus completeness & Erasing a boundary history can turn a
valid weighted statement into a false worst-case statement. & Retain a
conditionally sufficient boundary state and use positive transfer kernels.\\
\addlinespace
Local repair versus realizability & An operation local in staple space can
necessarily export curvature in link space. & Repair coordinated polymers or
use normalized integration without local repair.\\
\addlinespace
Energy versus entropy & An action barrier does not control normalized
probability when multiplicity and denominators compensate it. & Prove a
free-energy, relative-entropy, or partition-ratio inequality.\\
\addlinespace
Typicality versus hostile boundaries & Rare but positive-mass histories can
destroy a scalar conditional ceiling. & Use a state weight that transports
the cost of entering and persisting in hostile states.\\
\addlinespace
Continuous charts versus topology & Near-identity coordinates miss center
flux, cut/orbit transitions, and integer charge. & Use a typed multichannel
atlas and prove its closure under blocking.\\
\addlinespace
Finite exactness versus physical uniformity & A certified finite-block
spectrum need not survive volume, scale, or RG history. & Demand physical-unit
uniformity along the tuned continuum trajectory.\\
\addlinespace
Euclidean decay versus Hamiltonian spectrum & A stochastic or finite transfer
gap is not the Yang--Mills mass gap. & Preserve reflection positivity and a
dense physical observable core through OS reconstruction.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{What may and may not be compromised}

The non-negotiable content is a state-separating gauge-invariant observable
algebra, positivity sufficient for reconstruction, controlled locality in
physical distance, topological completeness, cutoff and volume uniformity,
and theory identity with nontrivial four-dimensional pure Yang--Mills.

The regulator, lattice action, microscopic gauge coordinates, a particular
block map, pointwise worst-boundary bounds, single-star repair, and premature
particle language may all be replaced.  The programme should preserve
phenomena and reconstruction certificates rather than a preferred set of
coordinates.
